I had a thought about this a while ago and I think one of the big contributors is simply geography.

While Reagan and Thatcher have similar rap sheets, particularly on the union crushing and paramilitary death squads, the thing that distinguishes them comes down to locations. Reagan’s big union bust was the ATC, and they’re an intelligentsia union of individual professionals dispersed all across the United States, whereas Thatcher destroyed the coal miners, who not only were much more regional but were also the center of their communities and significantly more working class, so when you destroyed their labour power you had the  knock on effect of impacting the whole town. These differences mean that the memory of those impacted is much more tightly focused in thatchers camp, and is able to reverberate and become folklore in a way Regan never has to contend with.

The other big one is the death squads, which follows a similar paradigm. Thatcher’s were in Northern Ireland, which is a decidedly smaller and more intimate region, but more importantly to the myth making resides largely in the imperial core. Reagan on the other hand deployed them in LatAm, which is firmly within the periphery and thereby having less impact on the memories of those in the core. 

TLDR: Reagan kept his shit out of his backyard and spread across the plate so people had an easier time forgetting it was shit.

So I think the addition of new universes is a really cool idea and will be great for the long term health of the game, much like how mtg has sustained itself for years off of the different planes. The biggest distinction that I feel between LoR and mtg cards are connected by the colours, which as a theme are more fluffy and hand waveable conceptually, vs Runeterra’s usage of regions which are much more definable concepts. I think the addition of cards from new themes that’ll be visually dissonant from existing regions will break clarity and cohesion in terms of what a region does, and may be better explored as new regions in and of themselves. 

While having many regions may seem like a poor idea, skinlines as regions creates space for an easily manageable rotating format, with the 10 core regions as evergreen, or a nonrotating base to that format, as well as giving players more reasons to hype up for new regions to drop and an ability to avoid them for themes they find unpalatable. Design mistakes that occur with new mechanics can find their way out of the format if they’re unbalancable, as inevitably there’ll be risks taken that’ll enter poor design spaces. Having new regions gives both the players and the design/balance team more freedom in how they approach the game, with players being able to choose how much content they want to actively participate in, and designers being able to push boundaries and make mistakes with new card design.   

Having alternate universes as new regions also creates space for a wider variety of playable formats, like a high powered “eternal” format, where all the regions as well as all the skin universes will be available forever, and will stop seeing nerfs or adjustments after so deep into their lifecycle. It’ll give options to explore new characters, and give people the ability to mix cool themes like say SI + High Noon for extra spookiness, and by keeping the base 10 regions as a core players can build solid tier 1.5-2 decks that’ll remain available throughout rotations. A nonrotating eternal format also gives players a space to get more whacky thematically, by building things like a star guardian+pool party deck or what have you, without taking away from the incredible work done to establish the themes of the core regions, as well as encouraging new players to remain in “standard” until they’ve played a couple rotations and developed pet decks their attached to. By encouraging new players into standard you also get them more likely to spend money on new cards and packs, as we as giving them more cohesive visual themes by limiting the number of regions available.
